text: Common mistakes Mistake Why it bites Do instead Comparing two models run in two different harnesses The harness alone moved our 4B model's success by tens of points Fix the harness to compare models; fix the model to compare harnesses (section 1) One rollout per cell Identical settings gave different outcomes; a single run cannot tell a harness effect from luck Several rollouts per task, a paired comparison over tasks, an interval Letting the workspace's tests decide the reward The agent can edit them, and the visible tests are a few examples of the spec Hidden checks, run outside the workspace, in a fresh container (sections 2 and 3) Fail-to-pass lists chosen by hand One bug can break checks in other functions (T04 broke six) Compute them by running every check on the buggy repository Ending the episode when a reply has no parsable tool call A malformed call looks like "done"; of our local rollouts ended that way, all failed Return the parse error as an observation and let the model retry; count these separately Training on groups where every reward is equal Zero advantage, zero gradient, full container cost Dynamic sampling, a partial reward, tasks near a 50% pass rate (section 4) Scoring a run that hit a cap as a plain failure Teaches the model that long attempts are bad rather than that the budget ran out Mask capped and timed-out rollouts (DeepSWE's compact filtering) Loss on tool output, or on re-rendered text Trains on tokens the policy did not sample (our template inserted 4 per rollout) Record token ids and log-probabilities at sampling time; mask observations (section 5) Publishing raw trajectories They carry paths, account names, ids, and sometimes credentials A whitelist redactor that fails closed (section 6) Trusting a self-improvement curve measured on the tuning tasks Best-of-many on a noisy score rises with no true gain Report held-out, out-of-distribution and other-executor numbers, with runs and intervals (section 7)
